live.instructions: BoB Tools — the signed-in user's own workspace: files (tables and forms), records, fields, views, share links and docs. START WITH bob_get_account. It returns the user's companies and files. IF THERE ARE NO FILES, the account is brand new — most likely created moments ago while connecting this connector — and there is nothing to query yet. Do not reply "you have no data" and stop. Offer to build something usable in one go: ask what the team collects in the field (orders, site visits, clients, inspections, deliveries), then create that table with bob_files, add its fields with bob_fields, and offer a public link with bob_shares so their team can start filling it in from their phones. Everything can be built from here — never send the user to the app to set things up first. ONCE THERE IS DATA: query and aggregate records (bob_records), group and filter through views (bob_views), read or attach record photos (bob_images), and assemble docs and dashboards from live records (bob_docs). Pictures in a doc go into its image storage — for files on disk get a URL with bob_docs upload_link and POST the bytes with curl (or hand the URL to the user to drop files), never paste base64 of a file — and are embedded in the text with ![caption](img:) in md or in html. TO REACH THE USER when background work is done or needs a decision, send a push to their own devices with bob_notify: title, text, what opens on tap, and up to three quick-answer buttons. Read the answer back with bob_notify get / list. Tools that modify or delete are annotated (destructiveHint) — confirm with the user before acting on those. AUTHENTICATION: OAuth 2.0 — the flow starts automatically on the first tool call. Clients that cannot run OAuth can instead send a token from https://web.bob.tools/#/mcp-auth ("Generate Token") in the Authorization header.

tools.name: bob_get_account
tools.title: Get account, companies and files
tools.description: Get account information: user email, companies with IDs, and list of files. By default returns personal files (up to 50) plus files from up to 5 companies (up to 50 each). Pass companyId to get only that company's files. Requires authentication.

companyId.description: Optional company ID to get only that company's files (up to 50). If not specified, returns personal files + files from up to 5 companies.

token.description: Session token, for clients that do not persist session headers.

tools.name: bob_files
tools.title: Manage files and folders
tools.description:
Manage files and folders.

Actions:
- list: List user's files. Params: companyId?, includeDeleted?, token?
- get: Get file details with fields, views, record count. Params: fileId, token?
- create: Create file or folder. Params: title, type?, fields?, companyId?, folderId?, description?, token?
- update: Update file title/description/folder. Params: fileId, title?, description?, folderId?
- delete: Soft-delete a file. Params: fileId
- move: Move files into a company or between folders. Params: fileIds, targetCompanyId?, targetFolderId?, dryRun?
  Company files never leave their company: omit targetCompanyId to keep each file where it is and
  only change its folder; pass it to move personal files in, or files from one company to another.

fileId.description: File ID (required for get, update, delete)

fileIds.description: File IDs to move (required for move)

companyId.description: Company ID (list: filter to company; create: create as company file)

title.description: File title (required for create, optional for update)

type.description: File type for create: 'form' (data file, default) or 'folder'

fields.description: Initial fields for create. Each: {title, type, subType?, elValues?, required?, ...}

targetCompanyId.description: Target company for move. Omit to keep each file where it is (personal stays personal, company files stay in their company) and only change the folder. Company files can never be moved to personal space.

targetFolderId.description: Target folder ID for move (must live in the destination space). Empty string moves to the root. Omit to keep the current folder (a cross-space move always lands in the root).

dryRun.description: Only validate the move without making changes (move; default: false)

token.description: Auth token for mobile clients (list, get, create)

tools.name: bob_records
tools.title: Query and edit records
tools.description:
Query, create, update, and delete records.

Actions:
- list: Get records with filtering/sorting/pagination. Params: fileId, filters?, sortBy?, sortOrder?, search?, deletedFilter?, limit?, offset?, recordIds?, expandReferences?, timezone?, viewId?, token?
- aggregate: Aggregate records (sum, count, avg, etc.). Params: fileId, groupByFieldIds?, aggregations, filters?, timezone?
- update: Update a single record. Params: fileId, recordId?, data, createIfNotFound?, validateOnly?
- update_many: Batch update multiple records. Params: fileId, updates[]
- delete: Delete a single record. Params: recordId
- delete_many: Delete multiple records. Params: fileId, recordIds[]
- history: Get record edit history. Params: fileId, recordId, limit?

Filter types: equals, notEquals, contains, notContains, multiSelect, dateRange, numberRange, isEmpty, isNotEmpty.
System fields for date filtering: dateCreated, dateUpdatedServer, dateSaved.

fileId.description: File ID (required for list, aggregate, update, update_many)

recordId.description: Record ID (update: optional if createIfNotFound, required for delete, history)

recordIds.description: Record IDs (list: fetch specific records; delete_many: required)

data.description: Field values as {fieldId: value} (required for update). Use field ID as key, string value.

updates.description: Batch updates for update_many. Each: {recordId?, data, createIfNotFound?}

filters.description: Query filters (list, aggregate). Each: {fieldId, type, value?, values?, from?, to?}

type.description: equals, notEquals, contains, notContains, multiSelect, dateRange, numberRange, isEmpty, isNotEmpty

sortBy.description: Field ID to sort by, or built-in: dateCreated, dateSaved, dateUpdatedServer (list)

sortOrder.description: Sort order: asc or desc (list; default: desc)

search.description: Text search across all fields including linked/referenced records (list; case-insensitive)

expandReferences.description: Show all fields of referenced records (list; default: false)

timezone.description: Timezone for date display (list, aggregate; e.g. 'Europe/London')

createIfNotFound.description: Create new record if recordId not provided or not found (update; default: false)

validateOnly.description: Only validate data without saving (update; default: false)

aggregations.description: Aggregation operations (required for aggregate). Each: {fieldId, operation: count/sum/avg/min/max/countDistinct}

tools.name: bob_fields
tools.title: Manage table fields
tools.description:
Manage fields in files.

Actions:
- add: Add field to a file. Params: fileId, title, type, subType?, required?, multiSelect?, elValues?, stateOnStart?, referenceFileId?, displayFieldsIn*?, formulaExpression?, lookupFileId?, lookupFieldId?, lookupDisplay*?, extractionFields?
- update: Update field settings. Params: fieldId, title?, type?, subType?, required?, multiSelect?, elValues?, stateOnStart?, referenceFileId?, displayFieldsIn*?, multiEntryEnabled?, multiEntryFieldIds?, formulaExpression?, lookupFileId?, lookupFieldId?, lookupDisplay*?, extractionFields?
- delete: Delete a field. Params: fieldId
- get_details: Get field details with options. Params: fieldId
- get_values: Get unique values for a field. Params: fileId, fieldId, limit?

Field types: textInput (with subType: number/float/longText/chips/lookup), dateInput, fileReference, chatReference, infoText, formula, signature, buttonQrCodeScan, photoAiProcess

fieldId.description: Field ID (required for update, delete, get_details, get_values)

title.description: Field title (required for add, optional for update)

type.description: Field type: textInput, dateInput, fileReference, chatReference, infoText, formula, signature, buttonQrCodeScan, photoAiProcess (required for add). Friendly aliases (text, number, float, select/dropdown, date, time, image/photo) are mapped to canonical types server-side; unknown types are rejected.

subType.description: For textInput: number, float, longText, chips, lookup

elValues.description: Options for chips. Each: {text, displayText?, color?, icon?}

color.description: Hex color for icon and chip (e.g., #4CAF50)

stateOnStart.description: Initial visibility: 'show' or 'hide' (for conditional visibility with actions)

referenceFileId.description: For fileReference: ID of the file to reference

displayFieldsInPopup.description: For fileReference: target-file field IDs shown when selecting a value. For chatReference: BobAssistantChat property names (customerName, customerPhone, lastMessagePreview, etc.). Always set displayFieldsInPopup/InForm/InList to human-readable fields (names, titles): with none configured the UI falls back to the first three fields of the target file, which are often technical IDs.

displayFieldsInList.description: For fileReference: target-file field IDs shown in table/list view. For chatReference: BobAssistantChat property names.

displayFieldsInForm.description: For fileReference: target-file field IDs shown in edit form. For chatReference: BobAssistantChat property names.

multiEntryEnabled.description: For fileReference (update): enable multi-entry mode — the selection popup lets the user type values (multiEntryFieldIds) per referenced record; on save the client creates one record per filled row. false disables.

multiEntryFieldIds.description: For fileReference with multiEntryEnabled (update): HOST-file field IDs editable inside the popup (e.g. hours, correction). Replaces the existing list.

lookupFieldId.description: For lookup: field ID to match against

lookupDisplayInPopup.description: For lookup: field IDs from target file to show in selection popup

lookupDisplayInList.description: For lookup: field IDs shown in list view

lookupDisplayInForm.description: For lookup: field IDs shown in form view

extractionFields.description: For photoAiProcess: AI extraction field names

subSettings.description:
Generic per-field extension settings. Keys are setting types; values are objects (currently only with intVal).

For action=add: the object becomes the field's initial map; only keys you list will be set.
For action=update: merge semantics — keys absent from the JSON are preserved, an object value upserts, and `null` removes that one key. `{}` is a no-op.

For dateInput, the date picker can be limited relative to today:
- "maxDaysBack" / "maxDaysForward" (intVal=N): general window; applies in the form and any share.
- "sharedMaxDaysBack" / "sharedMaxDaysForward" (intVal=N): only when opened via a share; combined with the general rule — strictest wins.

Example (update, set just one key without wiping others): { "subSettings": { "maxDaysBack": { "intVal": 7 } } }
Example (update, drop just one key): { "subSettings": { "sharedMaxDaysForward": null } }

tools.name: bob_images
tools.title: Record images: view and upload
tools.description: Manage images in records and docs. Actions: - get: Get image by ID as base64. Params: imageId, size? - add_to_record: Attach an image that is ALREADY in the same table and not held by another record to a record field. Params: recordId, fieldId, imageId. Images from a doc's storage, from another file or from another record are refused — a picture lives in one place; put a new copy into the record with action=upload. - upload: Upload new image from base64 data (for a FILE on disk that goes into a DOC use bob_docs action=upload_link and POST the file with curl, or hand the link to the user; a record field takes base64 only). Either into a RECORD field (params: recordId, fieldId, imageData, mimeType?; max side 1999 px; replaces the pictures already in the field) or into a DOC's image storage (params: docId, imageData, mimeType?, blockId?; large pictures are scaled down to 2000 px). The picture lands in the doc's IMAGE STORAGE (bob_docs action=images lists it, image_delete removes it). Show it inline right where it belongs: in an md block ![caption](img:), in an html block (bob_docs block_add/block_update); blockId appends it to an img gallery block instead. Never embed images as data: URIs in doc markdown — upload them here.

size.description: Image size for get action (default: full)

recordId.description: Record ID (required for add_to_record; upload into a record field)

fieldId.description: Field ID — photoAiProcess or signature field (required for add_to_record; upload into a record field)

docId.description: upload into a doc: the doc's file id (instead of recordId/fieldId). The image lands in the doc's storage and is referenced from Markdown as ![caption](img:<imageId>).

blockId.description: upload with docId: optionally an existing img block of that doc to append the image to

imageData.description: Base64-encoded image data without data: prefix (required for upload)

mimeType.description: Image MIME type for upload (default: image/jpeg)

tools.name: bob_shares
tools.title: Manage public share links
tools.description:
Manage file sharing and group shares.

Actions:
- list: List shares by file, company, or user. Params: fileId?, companyId?, includeDeleted?, limit?
- get: Get share details. Params: shareId
- create: Create a share link. Params: fileId (not needed for shareType=linkToGroup with groupShareId — an app entry link), shareType?, allowedOperations?, requirePin?, expirationHours?, viewId?, filters?, displayTitle?, showInList?, embedMode?, shareTheme?, showAllFields?, visibleFieldIds?, canAddData?, canEditData?, canViewData?, canDeleteData?, editData?, canAddRecordsInLink?, groupShareId?
- update: Update share settings. Params: shareId, allowedOperations?, requirePin?, expirationHours?, viewId?, filters?, deleted?, displayTitle?, showInList?, enabled?, embedMode?, shareTheme?, showAllFields?, visibleFieldIds?, canAddData?, canEditData?, canViewData?, canDeleteData?, editData?, canAddRecordsInLink?, fieldSettings?

fieldSettings (update): per-share field settings keyed by field ID; each listed field's entry is
replaced wholly (null removes it, unlisted fields keep theirs). An entry may contain
settingsOverride — a PARTIAL FieldSettings JSON that overrides the field's own settings in
this share only. Example (enable multi-entry input just for this share):
{"field_abc": {"settingsOverride": {"multiEntryEnabled": true, "multiEntryFieldIds": ["field_h", "field_c"]}}}
To force-disable: {"field_abc": {"settingsOverride": {"multiEntryEnabled": false}}}

Filter object schema: {fieldId, filterType: "equals"|"multiSelect"|"dateRange", value?, selectedValues?[], dateFrom?, dateTo?, isLocked?}
- delete: Soft-delete a share. Params: shareId
- get_pin: Get or regenerate share PIN. Params: shareId, regenerate?
A group share is a PORTAL: a page of buttons. A button opens either an existing linkShare on a
data file (linkShareId) or a doc/dashboard (docLinkId — a stable link from bob_docs
action=publish; it opens read-only inside the portal, the link itself stays non-public). Create
the linkShares / doc links first, then pass their IDs as buttons.
- create_group: Create group share (company-level). Params: title, companyId, buttons[], enabled?, embedMode?, shareTheme?
- get_group: Get group share details. Params: shareId
- update_group: Update group share. Params: shareId, title?, buttons? (replaces all), enabled?, embedMode?, shareTheme?, app?, accessMode?, blocklist?, allowlist?, allowDomains?, entryShareId?
  Users see a portal as an "app". app = its look, merged partially (null removes a key), e.g.
  {"app": {"accentColor": "#1E88E5", "iconText": "SK", "layout": "grid"}}. See the app parameter.
  Who may open the app is set on its ENTRY LINKS (linkToGroup / emailToGroup shares with groupShareId = this portal), not on the portal: accessMode / blocklist / allowlist / allowDomains apply to entryShareId if given, otherwise to every linkToGroup entry link of the portal (create one first with action=create, shareType=linkToGroup, groupShareId).

fileId.description: File ID (list: filter by file; create: required for linkShare, optional for linkToGroup with groupShareId)

companyId.description: Company ID (list: filter by company; create_group: required)

shareId.description: Share ID (required for get, update, delete, get_pin, get_group, update_group)

groupShareId.description: Group share this linkToGroup share belongs to (create)

title.description: Group share title (required for create_group, optional for update_group)

buttons.description: Portal buttons (create_group; update_group replaces all). Each button opens an existing linkShare (linkShareId) or a doc/dashboard stable link (docLinkId).

linkShareId.description: ID of the linkShare this button opens (data file). Use this OR docLinkId.

docLinkId.description: ID of a doc stable link (dashboardLink, from bob_docs action=publish). The button opens that doc/dashboard read-only inside the portal. Use this OR linkShareId.

folder.description: Folder path for grouping buttons (e.g. 'Reports/Monthly'). Use / for nesting. Optional.

shareType.description: Type of share: linkShare (public link) or linkToGroup (group access). Default: linkShare (create)

allowedOperations.description: Permissions: read (view only) or write (can edit). Default: read (create, update)

expirationHours.description: Expiration in hours from now (create, update)

viewId.description: View ID to use for shared display (create, update)

filters.description: Row-level filters for the share (create, update). Replaces all existing filters on update.

fieldId.description: Field ID to filter on (can include subfield: fieldId.subFieldId for fileReference fields)

isLocked.description: If true, user cannot change this filter. Default: false

displayTitle.description: Title shown to users viewing the share (create, update)

showInList.description: Whether to show in public shares list (create, update)

embedMode.description: If true, hides back button and navigation for iframe embedding (create, update)

shareTheme.description: Force theme: auto (system default), light, or dark (create, update)

showAllFields.description: Show all fields. Set to false and use visibleFieldIds to limit (create, update)

visibleFieldIds.description: Array of field IDs to show when showAllFields is false (create, update)

canAddData.description: Can users add new records (create, update)

canEditData.description: Which records can be edited: all, own (only own records), no (create, update)

canViewData.description: Data visibility: all or filtered (create, update)

editData.description: For linkShare: 'def' (form-only), 'viewFiltered' (can view list), 'editFiltered' (can view and edit list) (create, update)

canAddRecordsInLink.description: For linkShare: can users add new records (create, update)

fieldSettings.description: Per-share field settings keyed by field ID (update). Each value replaces that field's entry; null removes it. Supports settingsOverride: partial FieldSettings JSON overriding the field's own settings in this share only, e.g. {"field_abc": {"settingsOverride": {"multiEntryEnabled": true, "multiEntryFieldIds": ["field_h"]}}}

deleted.description: Set to false to restore a deleted share (update)

regenerate.description: Generate a new PIN (get_pin; default: false)

app.description:
update_group: The app's look (a portal is shown to users as an "app"). PARTIAL update: only the keys you pass change; a key set to null is removed (falls back to the default). Keys:
- name: app name in the header and under the home-screen icon (≤100 chars). Default: portal title.
- shortName: ≤12 chars, label under the installed icon. Default: name cut to 12.
- iconText: 1–3 letters/digits drawn on the accent colour when no icon image is set, e.g. "SK" or "3". Emoji, spaces and symbols are NOT supported. Default: initials of the name.
- iconImageId: image id (from bob_images / the company's image library) used as the app icon; null → drawn icon.
- accentColor: "#RRGGBB", colour of the header, buttons and the drawn icon.
- theme: auto | light | dark.
- coverImageId: image id shown as a cover above the buttons.
- welcomeText: markdown shown under the cover (≤5000 chars).
- layout: list | grid | tiles — how buttons are drawn.
- buttonSize: s | m | l.
- hideBranding: true hides the "Made with BoB" footer.
- locale: interface language for guests, e.g. "ru", "en".
- showInstall: true shows the "Install" button.
- allowClone: true lets visitors make their own copy of the app.

entryShareId.description: Entry link (linkToGroup / emailToGroup) of this portal that accessMode/blocklist/allowlist/allowDomains apply to. Default: all linkToGroup entry links of the portal (update_group)

accessMode.description: Who may open the app (update_group): open — anyone with the link; pin — anyone with the link's PIN (read it with get_pin on the entry link); login — any signed-in BoB account except the blocklist; allowlist — only emails in allowlist or domains in allowDomains. To drop a mode set "open".

blocklist.description: Emails or domains (@spam.ru) never let in, in any mode (update_group). Replaces the list; [] or null clears it.

allowlist.description: Emails let in when accessMode=allowlist (update_group). Replaces the list; [] or null clears it.

allowDomains.description: Domains let in when accessMode=allowlist, e.g. ["@firma.kz"]; exact domain, no subdomains (update_group). Replaces the list; [] or null clears it.

tools.name: bob_views
tools.title: Manage data views
tools.description:
Manage data views (table / timeAttendance / report).

Actions:
- list: List views for a file. Params: fileId, includeDeleted?, includeSettings?, viewId?
- create: Create a view. Params: fileId, title, type?, settings?
- update: Update view settings. Params: viewId, title?, settings?, replaceSettings?
  settings is a patch: only the top-level keys you pass change, null removes a key, the rest stays.
  A key's value is replaced whole (e.g. pass the full savedFilters array to add one preset).
- delete: Soft-delete a view. Params: viewId
- history: Get view edit history. Params: viewId, limit?

Dashboards are NOT views: charts, counters and cross-filtering live in doc files.
Use bob_docs to create a doc and add widget blocks to it.

Report view (type=report): settings IS the template, a JSON document rendered by the app to a
preview grid and exported to Excel with live formulas. Shape:
{"version":1,"title":"Act {actNumber} — {period}",
 "params":[{"id":"actNumber","type":"text"}],
 "dateField":"<fieldId>",                       // records outside the report period are dropped
 "columns":[{"id":"name","width":30,"header":"Item"},
            {"id":"day","repeat":"period.days","width":4,"header":"{day.n}"},   // one column per day of the period
            {"id":"total","header":"Total"},{"id":"rate"},{"id":"sum"}],
 "blocks":[{"type":"cells","rows":[[{"text":"{title}","span":"name:sum","style":"title"}]]},
           {"type":"header"},
           {"type":"table","id":"work",
            "rows":{"mode":"static","match":["<refFieldId>.<subFieldId>"],"matchMode":"contains",
                    "list":[{"key":["Day shift"],"cells":{"name":"Day works","rate":2050}}]},
            "cells":{"day":{"agg":"sum","field":"<hoursFieldId>"},"total":{"formula":"SUM(day)"},"sum":{"formula":"total*rate"}}},
           {"type":"row","id":"totals","cells":{"name":"Total","sum":{"formula":"SUM(work.sum)"}}},
           {"type":"row","id":"vat","cells":{"sum":{"formula":"totals.sum*0.22"}}},
           {"type":"spacer","rows":1}],
 "styles":{"title":{"bold":true,"align":"center","fontSize":12},"header":{"bold":true,"border":true}}}
Rules: rows mode "fromData" groups records by "groupBy" field paths (an empty list = no grouping,
one row for everything); "static" lists customer-dictated rows
matched by "match" field paths against each row's "key". Field paths are field IDs; "refFieldId.subFieldId"
follows a fileReference one level. Formulas are symbolic (column ids, block.column, SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX/COUNT/ROUND/ABS,
+ - * / and numbers) and become A1 formulas in Excel. Placeholders in text: {title} {period} {day.n} {param}.
A block id must not equal a column id. Style names must exist in "styles" ("header" styles the header row).
"locale":"ru"|"en" picks month/weekday names. Numbers must be JSON numbers (width, fontSize, value, rows).
Period: not a template param. The user picks it in the view's filter bar (arrows / date range, like the
time & attendance view); the template only names "dateField" and records outside the chosen period are
dropped, "period.days" columns follow it, {period} prints it. Do not add a "period" param (a legacy one
is accepted and ignored).
Filters: the template has none — record selection is the view's shared filter and its saved presets only
(the template cuts by the chosen period through "dateField"). Keys "defaultFilters" (object), "savedFilters" (array),
"filterDisplayMode" (string) and "visibleFilterFieldIds" (array) are those shared view filter settings,
not part of the template — pass them through unchanged.
Workflow for a report: read the file's fields (bob_fields) to get field IDs, sample a few records
(bob_records) to see real values for static-row keys and filters, create the view, then tell the
user to open it in the app: it shows a preview and exports .xlsx with formulas.

viewId.description: View ID (required for update, delete, history; list: show only this view, deleted or not)

type.description: View type for create: 'table' (default), 'timeAttendance' (pivot by day) or 'report' (JSON template → Excel with formulas)

settings.description: View settings object (create, update). For type=report this is the whole report template (see description). On update it is a patch: top-level keys you pass replace the stored ones, null removes a key, keys you omit are kept.

replaceSettings.description: update: replace the stored settings with 'settings' entirely instead of patching (default: false)

includeDeleted.description: Show deleted views for restoring (list; default: false)

includeSettings.description: Dump the raw viewSettings JSON of each view (list; default: false). To copy a view to another file, remap every field ID inside the dump (columns[].fieldId, dateField, rowField, summaryFields, visibleFilterFieldIds, ...) to the target file's own field IDs first — field IDs are globally unique, so a verbatim copy renders empty.

tools.name: bob_company
tools.title: Companies and invites
tools.description:
Manage companies and invitations.

Actions:
- create: Create a new company. Params: name, description?, maxUsers?
- enrollment_link: Create self-service enrollment link. Params: companyId, maxEnrollments?, roles?, expirationHours?, description?
- invite: Invite user to company. Params: companyId, userEmail, roles?

tools.name: bob_docs
tools.title: Manage block-based documents
tools.description:
Manage block-based documents shown in BoB Tools. A doc is owned by a company and is an ORDERED list of BLOCKS. Each block is Markdown ("md"), raw HTML ("html"), an image gallery ("img") or an interactive data widget ("widget"), max 32768 characters of content. Write in Markdown whenever possible — it renders cleanly and is easy to patch; use HTML only for things Markdown can't express. Editing ONE block touches only that block (not the whole doc), so prefer many small blocks over one giant block. The doc is served as a login-gated web page at https://api.bob.tools/d/{fileId}. MARKDOWN in md blocks is GitHub-flavored: tables and autolinks work. Raw HTML inside an md block is ESCAPED and shown as text, with ONE exception: a bare
(or
) is a line break. Use it for a line break inside a table cell (Markdown has no other way); it works anywhere in the text too, but not inside code spans or code fences. No attributes —
stays text; a line that STARTS with
is an HTML block and stays text too, so put it after some text. IMAGES: every doc has an IMAGE STORAGE — the doc's own list of pictures, independent of any block (the app shows it as the doc's "Images" panel). HOW TO GET A PICTURE IN: - a file on disk (screenshot, PNG from a folder, anything bigger than a few KB): call action=upload_link fileId={fileId} — it returns a one-day upload URL. If you can run shell commands, POST each file's raw bytes to it: curl --data-binary @picture.png → JSON with imageId and ready refs. If you can't, give the URL to the user: opened in a browser it is a drag-and-drop page. NEVER paste file bytes as base64 into a tool call for this — it truncates and fails; - a small picture you generated in memory: bob_images action=upload docId={fileId} imageData=. action=images lists the storage with each picture's size, the blocks that use it and ready-to-paste refs; action=image_delete removes one. Embed a stored picture right where it belongs in the text, like a figure in an article (the preferred way — no separate element needed): - md block: ![caption](img:) (a link [text](img:) opens the full picture); - html block (and custom widget markup): img: as a quoted attribute value or CSS url() — , , background:url(img:). The server rewrites it to the public image URL. Only ids from THIS doc's storage resolve. An "img" block (type=img, imageIds=[…], max 30) is an optional thumbnail gallery for a set of photos. Inline data:image URIs (base64 in md/html) and images from other docs are REJECTED. WIDGET blocks make a doc an interactive dashboard: first point the doc at a data file with set_dash, then add widget blocks. The viewer ships ONE compact dataset (only needed columns) and computes everything client-side: a doc-wide filter bar (date range + filter fields) plus CROSS-FILTERING — clicking a bar/pie segment/table row filters every other widget (with self-exclusion for the clicked widget). Zero backend cost per interaction; the dataset is cached server-side (dash.ttlSeconds). Docs containing widget blocks can NEVER be public — PIN and/or login only. Widget query JSON: {"widget":"counter|bar|pie|line|table|recordList", "agg":"count|sum|avg|min|max"?, "aggField":fieldId?, "groupBy":fieldId (bar/pie/line/table), "granularity":"day|week|month|year"? (line; default month), "limit":N?, "label":"…"? (counter), "columns":[fieldId,…]? (recordList), "sortBy":fieldId?, "sortDir":"asc|desc"?, "where":{fieldId:[values]}? (static widget-local filter), "link":{"bob":true}|{"template":"https://…/{fieldId}/…"}? (recordList row links; bob=true links to the record in BoB Tools), "rows":true? (custom renderer: also receive the matching data rows), "write":{...}? (custom renderer write-back, below)}. Values with a comma decimal separator are parsed. Fields with elValues display their displayText automatically. Custom rendering: pass content (html) WITH the query — it renders in a sandboxed iframe and receives {type:"bobWidgetData", value?/groups?, total, filter} via postMessage on every filter change; with "rows":true the payload also carries cols (column descriptors) and rows ([recordId, v1, v2, …] matching cols — sliced to query.columns when set, so list ONLY the fields the page may show). It may post back {type:"bobWidgetFilter", field?, value} to cross-filter the doc. Omit content for the built-in renderer. WRITE-BACK (custom renderers): "write":{"fields":[fieldId,…] (whitelist — the ONLY writable fields), "fileId":"file_…"? (target file, same company; default = dash.sourceFileId — so a widget can READ one table and WRITE to another), "allowCreate":bool? (default false = update-only), "reveal":{"fields":[fieldId,…], "fileId"?: where those records live (default = write target), "recordIdFrom"?: fieldId of the WRITTEN data whose value is the record id to reveal (default = the written record itself)}?}. The sandbox posts {type:"bobWidgetWrite", requestId?, recordId? (omit +create for a new record), data:{fieldId:value}} and receives {type:"bobWidgetWriteResult", requestId, ok, recordId?, reveal?, error?, local?} (local:true = the BoB Tools app saved it on the device, offline-capable; it reaches the server on the next sync). reveal fields NEVER ship with the dataset — they return only after a successful write (quiz semantics: the correct answer is not in the browser until the user has answered; also: reveal a contact after a request is claimed, a price after confirmation). Writes are validated server-side against the block's stored grant (whitelisted fields only — anything else errors), rate-limited, and attributed (login uid, or the link whose PIN was used). This makes docs a platform for interactive mini-apps: quizzes, approve/reject buttons, checklists, inline status changes. Actions: - create: Make a new empty doc. Args: companyId, title. Returns fileId + URL. - list: List a company's docs. Args: companyId. - get: Get a doc as an OUTLINE — its ordered blocks by header only (custom header, else the block's first line), plus URL, stable links, shares, access, dash config. Then read the block you actually need with get_block. Args: fileId, blockDetail? ("titles" = headers only, the default; "preview" = header + ~80 chars; "full" = complete content of every block — expensive on a long doc). - images: List the doc's image storage — every picture with its id, size, the blocks that use it and ready-to-paste md/html refs. Args: fileId. - upload_link: Get a one-day upload URL for the doc's image storage (see IMAGES). POST raw image bytes to it (curl --data-binary @file.png URL, one file per request, JPEG/PNG/GIF/BMP, max 15 MB, scaled to 2000 px) or open it in a browser to drop files. The URL is a credential for adding pictures to THIS doc — share it only with people who may edit the doc. Args: fileId. - image_delete: Remove a picture from the doc's storage (its bytes are deleted). Refused while a block still references it unless force=true. Args: fileId, imageId, force?. - get_block: Get ONE block's complete content/type/query/header verbatim (this is the cheap way to read content — one block instead of the whole doc). Args: blockId. - search: Find blocks by text in their headers and content, across one doc or every doc of a company. Returns the matching blocks (doc, blockId, header, snippet) — read one with get_block. Args: search (the text), fileId? (one doc) or companyId? (all docs of the company), limit? (default 20, max 100). - set_dash: Configure the doc's widget data source. Args: docId, dash = JSON {"sourceFileId":"file_…" (same company), "dateField":fieldId?, "filterFields":[fieldId,…]?, "maxRows":N? (default 5000, max 20000), "ttlSeconds":N? (dataset cache, default 300)}. - block_add: Append or insert a block. Args: docId, type (md|html|img|widget), content (md/html markup; for widget: optional custom renderer html), query (widget only: the JSON spec above), imageIds (img only: ids from bob_images upload docId=…), blockTitle? (header shown above the block), collapsed? (start folded under the header), afterBlockId? (insert right after this block; omit to append at the end). Returns the new blockId. - block_update: Change a block's content/type/query/images/header in place. Args: blockId, content?, type?, query?, imageIds? (img only: REPLACES the block's image list — pass the full list, e.g. to reorder or drop one), blockTitle? (empty string removes the header), collapsed?. - block_rename: Change ONLY a block's header, never its content — the safe way to retitle. Args: blockId, blockTitle (empty string drops the custom header, so it falls back to the block's first line; the header row and collapse flag stay as they are). - block_delete: Remove a block. Args: blockId. - reorder: Set the full block order. Args: docId, orderedBlockIds (array of every block id in the desired order). - publish: Create or re-point a STABLE link (a permanent /d/s/{linkId} URL that survives re-pointing). Args: fileId, linkId?. - share: Email-invite someone to view the doc. Args: fileId, email. - set_access: Configure how viewers open the doc or a stable link. public=true makes it open for ANYONE with the URL (no login/PIN; refused for docs with widget blocks); pin (6–12 digits) enables PIN entry (empty string removes it); login (default true) toggles Google/email sign-in. At least one method must stay enabled. Args: fileId|linkId, public?, pin?, login?. - delete: Soft-delete the doc, its blocks, and any stable links/shares pointing at it. Args: fileId.

tools.name: bob_notify
tools.title: Notifications to the user
tools.description:
Send a push notification to the signed-in user's own devices (BoB Tools app on phone and web) and read back how they answered.

Use it when you finish background work and need the user's attention or a quick decision — e.g. "3 new leads found", "report is ready", "approve this reply?". Only the user who owns this connection is notified; other people cannot be targeted.

What the user sees: a system notification with your title and body. Tapping it opens the target you set (a doc/dashboard, a table, a record, or a link). On Android and web your action buttons appear on the notification itself; on iOS they appear in the app after the tap. Every notification is also kept in the app's notifications feed, so it is not lost if the push is missed.

Actions:
- send: Push a notification. Params: title, body?, one target of fileId | lineId | url, actions?, reply?, thread?
  Returns notificationId and how many devices were reached. If 0 devices have notifications enabled, the notification is still stored in the feed — tell the user to open the BoB Tools app and allow notifications.
- list: Your notification history, newest first, with read state and the user's answers. Params: thread?, status?, archived?, sinceMs?, beforeMs?, limit? When the result has hasMore=true, call again with beforeMs=nextBeforeMs for the older ones. status=pending returns only questions still waiting for the user — not answered, not resolved, not info. Archived ones are left out unless archived=only or include.
- get: One notification and its answer. Params: notificationId. Returns immediately — it never waits.
- resolve: Close a notification once the matter is settled, with a short note on how it ended. Params: notificationId, note? (up to 500 chars, e.g. "applied", "handled by phone", "no longer relevant"). The buttons and the reply field disappear in the app, the system notification is withdrawn from the user's phones, and a late tap is refused; an answer the user already gave is kept. Its status becomes resolved and it no longer appears in list status=pending. Calling it again only replaces the note. Use it whenever a question you asked stops needing an answer — do not leave it pending.
- update: Change a notification you already sent — new status, text, target or buttons — instead of sending a new one. Params: notificationId? (omitted = your latest sent notification, or the latest in thread if you pass thread — then thread selects the notification and is not changed), then any of title, body, fileId | lineId | url, actions, reply, thread (fields you leave out stay as they are; at least one is required). The result always names the notificationId it updated. The user's devices replace the old notification in place, it becomes unread again, and the previous version is kept in its history (returned by get). If the buttons or the reply mode really change, the user's earlier answer is cleared so they can answer again (the old answer stays in history); passing the same buttons again with a new text keeps the answer. Counts toward the send limit.
  IMPORTANT: to report progress or a new status of something you already notified about ("scan started" → "scan done: 3 leads"), call update with that notificationId — do NOT call send again, or the user gets duplicate notifications.
- archive: Clean up the user's feed — move notifications that no longer need attention but are worth keeping (a done report, a settled question, a past result) out of the feed into the archive. Params: notificationIds (up to 100) or notificationId, note? (why, up to 500 chars). A pending question is also resolved, as with resolve; an answer is kept. Still readable with get and list archived=only. An update brings an archived notification back to the feed.
- unarchive: Return archived notifications to the feed. Params: notificationIds or notificationId.
- delete: Remove worthless notifications for good — duplicates, test pings, stale progress messages nobody needs to see again. Params: notificationIds (up to 100) or notificationId. They disappear from the feed, from list and get, and from the user's phones. Prefer archive when in doubt.
  archive, unarchive and delete return a result per id (ok, unchanged, not_found, not_bob_notify, deleted); one call counts as one write however many ids it names.

Status of every notification (get, list): pending — a question (buttons or reply) still waiting; answered — the user answered; info — no buttons and no reply, nothing was asked, nothing to wait for; resolved — you closed it with resolve (a kept answer is still in response). An update that changes the buttons or the reply mode asks anew and reopens a resolved notification.

Reading the answer: a tap on a button or a typed reply is recorded once (first answer wins). `response.actionId` is the id of the button you defined; `response.text` is the free-text reply. The user may answer much later, so do not block on it: call get every 15 seconds for the first 2 minutes after sending, then once a minute until 10 minutes, then once every 5 minutes (an unanswered get tells you the notification's age and when to check next), or — for a background job — skip the polling and call list status=answered with your thread on the next tick. Every get counts toward the daily tool-call limit like any other call.

thread: your own tag for a series of notifications (e.g. "upwork-scan"). Reuse the same tag on every run so list(thread=...) returns just that series and its answers.

Limit: 30 writes (send, update, resolve, archive, unarchive, delete) and 600 list/get reads per hour. bob_notify calls are free: they do not count toward the daily MCP limit and keep working after it is used up.

Each: {id, label, url?}. id: your own key, 1-40 chars of a-z 0-9 _ - , unique — it comes back as response.actionId. label: button text, up to 30 chars. url: optional https link the button also opens.

Generic per-field extension settings. Keys are setting types; values are objects (currently only with intVal).

For dateInput, the date picker can be limited relative to today:
- "maxDaysBack" / "maxDaysForward" (intVal=N): general window; applies in the form and any share.
- "sharedMaxDaysBack" / "sharedMaxDaysForward" (intVal=N): only when opened via a share; combined with the general rule — strictest wins.

The picture lands in the doc's IMAGE STORAGE (bob_docs action=images lists it, image_delete removes it). Show it inline right where it belongs: in an md block ![caption](img:), in an html block (bob_docs block_add/block_update); blockId appends it to an img gallery block instead. settingsOverride — a PARTIAL FieldSettings JSON that overrides the field's own settings in
this share only. Example (enable multi-entry input just for this share):
{"field_abc": {"settingsOverride": {"multiEntryEnabled": true, "multiEntryFieldIds": ["field_h", "field_c"]}}}
To force-disable: {"field_abc": {"settingsOverride": {"multiEntryEnabled": false}}}

Filter object schema: {fieldId, filterType: "equals"|"multiSelect"|"dateRange", value?, selectedValues?[], dateFrom?, dateTo?, isLocked?}
- delete: Soft-delete a share. Params: shareId
- get_pin: Get or regenerate share PIN. Params: shareId, regenerate?
A group share is a PORTAL: a page of buttons. A button opens either an existing linkShare on a
data file (linkShareId) or a doc/dashboard (docLinkId — a stable link from bob_docs
action=publish; it opens read-only inside the portal, the link itself stays non-public). Create
the linkShares / doc links first, then pass their IDs as buttons.
- create_group: Create group share (company-level). Params: title, companyId, buttons[], enabled?, embedMode?, shareTheme?
- get_group: Get group share details. Params: shareId
- update_group: Update group share. Params: shareId, title?, buttons? (replaces all), enabled?, embedMode?, shareTheme?, app?, accessMode?, blocklist?, allowlist?, allowDomains?, entryShareId?
  Users see a portal as an "app". app = its look, merged partially (null removes a key), e.g.
  {"app": {"accentColor": "#1E88E5", "iconText": "SK", "layout": "grid"}}. See the app parameter.
  Who may open the app is set on its ENTRY LINKS (linkToGroup / emailToGroup shares with groupShareId = this portal), not on the portal: accessMode / blocklist / allowlist / allowDomains apply to entryShareId if given, otherwise to every linkToGroup entry link of the portal (create one first with action=create, shareType=linkToGroup, groupShareId).

fileId.description: File ID (list: filter by file; create: required for linkShare, optional for linkToGroup with groupShareId)

companyId.description: Company ID (list: filter by company; create_group: required)

shareId.description: Share ID (required for get, update, delete, get_pin, get_group, update_group)

groupShareId.description: Group share this linkToGroup share belongs to (create)

title.description: Group share title (required for create_group, optional for update_group)

buttons.description: Portal buttons (create_group; update_group replaces all). Each button opens an existing linkShare (linkShareId) or a doc/dashboard stable link (docLinkId).

linkShareId.description: ID of the linkShare this button opens (data file). Use this OR docLinkId.

docLinkId.description: ID of a doc stable link (dashboardLink, from bob_docs action=publish). The button opens that doc/dashboard read-only inside the portal. Use this OR linkShareId.

folder.description: Folder path for grouping buttons (e.g. 'Reports/Monthly'). Use / for nesting. Optional.

shareType.description: Type of share: linkShare (public link) or linkToGroup (group access). Default: linkShare (create)

allowedOperations.description: Permissions: read (view only) or write (can edit). Default: read (create, update)

expirationHours.description: Expiration in hours from now (create, update)

viewId.description: View ID to use for shared display (create, update)

filters.description: Row-level filters for the share (create, update). Replaces all existing filters on update.

fieldId.description: Field ID to filter on (can include subfield: fieldId.subFieldId for fileReference fields)

isLocked.description: If true, user cannot change this filter. Default: false

displayTitle.description: Title shown to users viewing the share (create, update)

showInList.description: Whether to show in public shares list (create, update)

embedMode.description: If true, hides back button and navigation for iframe embedding (create, update)

shareTheme.description: Force theme: auto (system default), light, or dark (create, update)

showAllFields.description: Show all fields. Set to false and use visibleFieldIds to limit (create, update)

visibleFieldIds.description: Array of field IDs to show when showAllFields is false (create, update)

canAddData.description: Can users add new records (create, update)

canEditData.description: Which records can be edited: all, own (only own records), no (create, update)

canViewData.description: Data visibility: all or filtered (create, update)

editData.description: For linkShare: 'def' (form-only), 'viewFiltered' (can view list), 'editFiltered' (can view and edit list) (create, update)

canAddRecordsInLink.description: For linkShare: can users add new records (create, update)

fieldSettings.description: Per-share field settings keyed by field ID (update). Each value replaces that field's entry; null removes it. Supports settingsOverride: partial FieldSettings JSON overriding the field's own settings in this share only, e.g. {"field_abc": {"settingsOverride": {"multiEntryEnabled": true, "multiEntryFieldIds": ["field_h"]}}}

deleted.description: Set to false to restore a deleted share (update)

regenerate.description: Generate a new PIN (get_pin; default: false)

app.description:
update_group: The app's look (a portal is shown to users as an "app"). PARTIAL update: only the keys you pass change; a key set to null is removed (falls back to the default). Keys:
- name: app name in the header and under the home-screen icon (≤100 chars). Default: portal title.
- shortName: ≤12 chars, label under the installed icon. Default: name cut to 12.
- iconText: 1–3 letters/digits drawn on the accent colour when no icon image is set, e.g. "SK" or "3". Emoji, spaces and symbols are NOT supported. Default: initials of the name.
- iconImageId: image id (from bob_images / the company's image library) used as the app icon; null → drawn icon.
- accentColor: "#RRGGBB", colour of the header, buttons and the drawn icon.
- theme: auto | light | dark.
- coverImageId: image id shown as a cover above the buttons.
- welcomeText: markdown shown under the cover (≤5000 chars).
- layout: list | grid | tiles — how buttons are drawn.
- buttonSize: s | m | l.
- hideBranding: true hides the "Made with BoB" footer.
- locale: interface language for guests, e.g. "ru", "en".
- showInstall: true shows the "Install" button.
- allowClone: true lets visitors make their own copy of the app.

entryShareId.description: Entry link (linkToGroup / emailToGroup) of this portal that accessMode/blocklist/allowlist/allowDomains apply to. Default: all linkToGroup entry links of the portal (update_group)

accessMode.description: Who may open the app (update_group): open — anyone with the link; pin — anyone with the link's PIN (read it with get_pin on the entry link); login — any signed-in BoB account except the blocklist; allowlist — only emails in allowlist or domains in allowDomains. To drop a mode set "open".

blocklist.description: Emails or domains (@spam.ru) never let in, in any mode (update_group). Replaces the list; [] or null clears it.

allowlist.description: Emails let in when accessMode=allowlist (update_group). Replaces the list; [] or null clears it.

allowDomains.description: Domains let in when accessMode=allowlist, e.g. ["@firma.kz"]; exact domain, no subdomains (update_group). Replaces the list; [] or null clears it.

tools.name: bob_views
tools.title: Manage data views
tools.description:
Manage data views (table / timeAttendance / report).

Actions:
- list: List views for a file. Params: fileId, includeDeleted?, includeSettings?, viewId?
- create: Create a view. Params: fileId, title, type?, settings?
- update: Update view settings. Params: viewId, title?, settings?, replaceSettings?
  settings is a patch: only the top-level keys you pass change, null removes a key, the rest stays.
  A key's value is replaced whole (e.g. pass the full savedFilters array to add one preset).
- delete: Soft-delete a view. Params: viewId
- history: Get view edit history. Params: viewId, limit?

Dashboards are NOT views: charts, counters and cross-filtering live in doc files.
Use bob_docs to create a doc and add widget blocks to it.

Report view (type=report): settings IS the template, a JSON document rendered by the app to a
preview grid and exported to Excel with live formulas. Shape:
{"version":1,"title":"Act {actNumber} — {period}",
 "params":[{"id":"actNumber","type":"text"}],
 "dateField":"<fieldId>",                       // records outside the report period are dropped
 "columns":[{"id":"name","width":30,"header":"Item"},
            {"id":"day","repeat":"period.days","width":4,"header":"{day.n}"},   // one column per day of the period
            {"id":"total","header":"Total"},{"id":"rate"},{"id":"sum"}],
 "blocks":[{"type":"cells","rows":[[{"text":"{title}","span":"name:sum","style":"title"}]]},
           {"type":"header"},
           {"type":"table","id":"work",
            "rows":{"mode":"static","match":["<refFieldId>.<subFieldId>"],"matchMode":"contains",
                    "list":[{"key":["Day shift"],"cells":{"name":"Day works","rate":2050}}]},
            "cells":{"day":{"agg":"sum","field":"<hoursFieldId>"},"total":{"formula":"SUM(day)"},"sum":{"formula":"total*rate"}}},
           {"type":"row","id":"totals","cells":{"name":"Total","sum":{"formula":"SUM(work.sum)"}}},
           {"type":"row","id":"vat","cells":{"sum":{"formula":"totals.sum*0.22"}}},
           {"type":"spacer","rows":1}],
 "styles":{"title":{"bold":true,"align":"center","fontSize":12},"header":{"bold":true,"border":true}}}
Rules: rows mode "fromData" groups records by "groupBy" field paths (an empty list = no grouping,
one row for everything); "static" lists customer-dictated rows
matched by "match" field paths against each row's "key". Field paths are field IDs; "refFieldId.subFieldId"
follows a fileReference one level. Formulas are symbolic (column ids, block.column, SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX/COUNT/ROUND/ABS,
+ - * / and numbers) and become A1 formulas in Excel. Placeholders in text: {title} {period} {day.n} {param}.
A block id must not equal a column id. Style names must exist in "styles" ("header" styles the header row).
"locale":"ru"|"en" picks month/weekday names. Numbers must be JSON numbers (width, fontSize, value, rows).
Period: not a template param. The user picks it in the view's filter bar (arrows / date range, like the
time & attendance view); the template only names "dateField" and records outside the chosen period are
dropped, "period.days" columns follow it, {period} prints it. Do not add a "period" param (a legacy one
is accepted and ignored).
Filters: the template has none — record selection is the view's shared filter and its saved presets only
(the template cuts by the chosen period through "dateField"). Keys "defaultFilters" (object), "savedFilters" (array),
"filterDisplayMode" (string) and "visibleFilterFieldIds" (array) are those shared view filter settings,
not part of the template — pass them through unchanged.
Workflow for a report: read the file's fields (bob_fields) to get field IDs, sample a few records
(bob_records) to see real values for static-row keys and filters, create the view, then tell the
user to open it in the app: it shows a preview and exports .xlsx with formulas.

viewId.description: View ID (required for update, delete, history; list: show only this view, deleted or not)

type.description: View type for create: 'table' (default), 'timeAttendance' (pivot by day) or 'report' (JSON template → Excel with formulas)

settings.description: View settings object (create, update). For type=report this is the whole report template (see description). On update it is a patch: top-level keys you pass replace the stored ones, null removes a key, keys you omit are kept.

replaceSettings.description: update: replace the stored settings with 'settings' entirely instead of patching (default: false)

includeDeleted.description: Show deleted views for restoring (list; default: false)

includeSettings.description: Dump the raw viewSettings JSON of each view (list; default: false). To copy a view to another file, remap every field ID inside the dump (columns[].fieldId, dateField, rowField, summaryFields, visibleFilterFieldIds, ...) to the target file's own field IDs first — field IDs are globally unique, so a verbatim copy renders empty.

tools.name: bob_company
tools.title: Companies and invites
tools.description:
Manage companies and invitations.

Actions:
- create: Create a new company. Params: name, description?, maxUsers?
- enrollment_link: Create self-service enrollment link. Params: companyId, maxEnrollments?, roles?, expirationHours?, description?
- invite: Invite user to company. Params: companyId, userEmail, roles?

tools.name: bob_docs
tools.title: Manage block-based documents
tools.description:
Manage block-based documents shown in BoB Tools. A doc is owned by a company and is an ORDERED list of BLOCKS. Each block is Markdown ("md"), raw HTML ("html"), an image gallery ("img") or an interactive data widget ("widget"), max 32768 characters of content. Write in Markdown whenever possible — it renders cleanly and is easy to patch; use HTML only for things Markdown can't express. Editing ONE block touches only that block (not the whole doc), so prefer many small blocks over one giant block. The doc is served as a login-gated web page at https://api.bob.tools/d/{fileId}. MARKDOWN in md blocks is GitHub-flavored: tables and autolinks work. Raw HTML inside an md block is ESCAPED and shown as text, with ONE exception: a bare
(or
) is a line break. Use it for a line break inside a table cell (Markdown has no other way); it works anywhere in the text too, but not inside code spans or code fences. No attributes —
stays text; a line that STARTS with
is an HTML block and stays text too, so put it after some text. IMAGES: every doc has an IMAGE STORAGE — the doc's own list of pictures, independent of any block (the app shows it as the doc's "Images" panel). HOW TO GET A PICTURE IN: - a file on disk (screenshot, PNG from a folder, anything bigger than a few KB): call action=upload_link fileId={fileId} — it returns a one-day upload URL. If you can run shell commands, POST each file's raw bytes to it: curl --data-binary @picture.png → JSON with imageId and ready refs. If you can't, give the URL to the user: opened in a browser it is a drag-and-drop page. NEVER paste file bytes as base64 into a tool call for this — it truncates and fails; - a small picture you generated in memory: bob_images action=upload docId={fileId} imageData=. action=images lists the storage with each picture's size, the blocks that use it and ready-to-paste refs; action=image_delete removes one. Embed a stored picture right where it belongs in the text, like a figure in an article (the preferred way — no separate element needed): - md block: ![caption](img:) (a link [text](img:) opens the full picture); - html block (and custom widget markup): img: as a quoted attribute value or CSS url() — , , background:url(img:). The server rewrites it to the public image URL. Only ids from THIS doc's storage resolve. An "img" block (type=img, imageIds=[…], max 30) is an optional thumbnail gallery for a set of photos. Inline data:image URIs (base64 in md/html) and images from other docs are REJECTED. WIDGET blocks make a doc an interactive dashboard: first point the doc at a data file with set_dash, then add widget blocks. The viewer ships ONE compact dataset (only needed columns) and computes everything client-side: a doc-wide filter bar (date range + filter fields) plus CROSS-FILTERING — clicking a bar/pie segment/table row filters every other widget (with self-exclusion for the clicked widget). Zero backend cost per interaction; the dataset is cached server-side (dash.ttlSeconds). Docs containing widget blocks can NEVER be public — PIN and/or login only. Widget query JSON: {"widget":"counter|bar|pie|line|table|recordList", "agg":"count|sum|avg|min|max"?, "aggField":fieldId?, "groupBy":fieldId (bar/pie/line/table), "granularity":"day|week|month|year"? (line; default month), "limit":N?, "label":"…"? (counter), "columns":[fieldId,…]? (recordList), "sortBy":fieldId?, "sortDir":"asc|desc"?, "where":{fieldId:[values]}? (static widget-local filter), "link":{"bob":true}|{"template":"https://…/{fieldId}/…"}? (recordList row links; bob=true links to the record in BoB Tools), "rows":true? (custom renderer: also receive the matching data rows), "write":{...}? (custom renderer write-back, below)}. Values with a comma decimal separator are parsed. Fields with elValues display their displayText automatically. Custom rendering: pass content (html) WITH the query — it renders in a sandboxed iframe and receives {type:"bobWidgetData", value?/groups?, total, filter} via postMessage on every filter change; with "rows":true the payload also carries cols (column descriptors) and rows ([recordId, v1, v2, …] matching cols — sliced to query.columns when set, so list ONLY the fields the page may show). It may post back {type:"bobWidgetFilter", field?, value} to cross-filter the doc. Omit content for the built-in renderer. WRITE-BACK (custom renderers): "write":{"fields":[fieldId,…] (whitelist — the ONLY writable fields), "fileId":"file_…"? (target file, same company; default = dash.sourceFileId — so a widget can READ one table and WRITE to another), "allowCreate":bool? (default false = update-only), "reveal":{"fields":[fieldId,…], "fileId"?: where those records live (default = write target), "recordIdFrom"?: fieldId of the WRITTEN data whose value is the record id to reveal (default = the written record itself)}?}. The sandbox posts {type:"bobWidgetWrite", requestId?, recordId? (omit +create for a new record), data:{fieldId:value}} and receives {type:"bobWidgetWriteResult", requestId, ok, recordId?, reveal?, error?, local?} (local:true = the BoB Tools app saved it on the device, offline-capable; it reaches the server on the next sync). reveal fields NEVER ship with the dataset — they return only after a successful write (quiz semantics: the correct answer is not in the browser until the user has answered; also: reveal a contact after a request is claimed, a price after confirmation). Writes are validated server-side against the block's stored grant (whitelisted fields only — anything else errors), rate-limited, and attributed (login uid, or the link whose PIN was used). This makes docs a platform for interactive mini-apps: quizzes, approve/reject buttons, checklists, inline status changes. Actions: - create: Make a new empty doc. Args: companyId, title. Returns fileId + URL. - list: List a company's docs. Args: companyId. - get: Get a doc as an OUTLINE — its ordered blocks by header only (custom header, else the block's first line), plus URL, stable links, shares, access, dash config. Then read the block you actually need with get_block. Args: fileId, blockDetail? ("titles" = headers only, the default; "preview" = header + ~80 chars; "full" = complete content of every block — expensive on a long doc). - images: List the doc's image storage — every picture with its id, size, the blocks that use it and ready-to-paste md/html refs. Args: fileId. - upload_link: Get a one-day upload URL for the doc's image storage (see IMAGES). POST raw image bytes to it (curl --data-binary @file.png URL, one file per request, JPEG/PNG/GIF/BMP, max 15 MB, scaled to 2000 px) or open it in a browser to drop files. The URL is a credential for adding pictures to THIS doc — share it only with people who may edit the doc. Args: fileId. - image_delete: Remove a picture from the doc's storage (its bytes are deleted). Refused while a block still references it unless force=true. Args: fileId, imageId, force?. - get_block: Get ONE block's complete content/type/query/header verbatim (this is the cheap way to read content — one block instead of the whole doc). Args: blockId. - search: Find blocks by text in their headers and content, across one doc or every doc of a company. Returns the matching blocks (doc, blockId, header, snippet) — read one with get_block. Args: search (the text), fileId? (one doc) or companyId? (all docs of the company), limit? (default 20, max 100). - set_dash: Configure the doc's widget data source. Args: docId, dash = JSON {"sourceFileId":"file_…" (same company), "dateField":fieldId?, "filterFields":[fieldId,…]?, "maxRows":N? (default 5000, max 20000), "ttlSeconds":N? (dataset cache, default 300)}. - block_add: Append or insert a block. Args: docId, type (md|html|img|widget), content (md/html markup; for widget: optional custom renderer html), query (widget only: the JSON spec above), imageIds (img only: ids from bob_images upload docId=…), blockTitle? (header shown above the block), collapsed? (start folded under the header), afterBlockId? (insert right after this block; omit to append at the end). Returns the new blockId. - block_update: Change a block's content/type/query/images/header in place. Args: blockId, content?, type?, query?, imageIds? (img only: REPLACES the block's image list — pass the full list, e.g. to reorder or drop one), blockTitle? (empty string removes the header), collapsed?. - block_rename: Change ONLY a block's header, never its content — the safe way to retitle. Args: blockId, blockTitle (empty string drops the custom header, so it falls back to the block's first line; the header row and collapse flag stay as they are). - block_delete: Remove a block. Args: blockId. - reorder: Set the full block order. Args: docId, orderedBlockIds (array of every block id in the desired order). - publish: Create or re-point a STABLE link (a permanent /d/s/{linkId} URL that survives re-pointing). Args: fileId, linkId?. - share: Email-invite someone to view the doc. Args: fileId, email. - set_access: Configure how viewers open the doc or a stable link. public=true makes it open for ANYONE with the URL (no login/PIN; refused for docs with widget blocks); pin (6–12 digits) enables PIN entry (empty string removes it); login (default true) toggles Google/email sign-in. At least one method must stay enabled. Args: fileId|linkId, public?, pin?, login?. - delete: Soft-delete the doc, its blocks, and any stable links/shares pointing at it. Args: fileId.

companyId.description: Company ID that owns the doc (required for create/list)

imageId.description: image_delete: id of the picture to remove from the doc's image storage

force.description: image_delete: delete even while blocks still reference the image (default false)

docId.description: Doc file ID a block belongs to (block_add/reorder)

blockDetail.description: get: how much of each block to return — titles (headers only, the default), preview (header + ~80 chars), full (complete content of every block; expensive — prefer get_block)

fullContent.description: get: legacy alias for blockDetail=full (default false)

search.description: search: text to look for in block headers and content (case-insensitive substring, min 2 chars)

limit.description: search: max matching blocks to return (default 20, max 100)

linkId.description: Stable link ID (/d/s/{linkId}). publish: omit to create, pass to re-point. set_access: configure the link instead of the file.

type.description: Block type (block_add/block_update): md = Markdown, html = raw HTML, img = image gallery (imageIds), widget = interactive data widget

content.description: Block text — Markdown or HTML, max 32768 chars (block_add/block_update). For widget blocks: optional custom renderer HTML (omit for the built-in renderer). Ignored for img blocks.

query.description: Widget blocks only: the widget's JSON query spec (see tool description), max 4096 chars (block_add/block_update)

imageIds.description: img blocks only: image ids returned by bob_images action=upload docId=… for THIS doc, in display order, max 30. block_add: required for type=img. block_update: replaces the whole list.

blockTitle.description: block_add/block_update/block_rename: header text rendered above the block (collapsible <details>). On block_add/block_update an empty string removes the header entirely (and un-collapses); on block_rename it only drops the custom text, so the header falls back to the block's first line. Blocks marked fullscreen in the app keep a header regardless.

collapsed.description: block_add/block_update: true folds the block under its header by default (viewer can expand); the header text is blockTitle, else the block's first line. false unfolds a previously collapsed block (its header stays, expanded); on a block that was never collapsed it is a no-op.

dash.description: set_dash: JSON dash config — sourceFileId (required, same company), dateField?, filterFields?, maxRows?, ttlSeconds?

afterBlockId.description: block_add: insert the new block right after this block; omit to append at the end

orderedBlockIds.description: reorder: every block id of the doc in the desired top-to-bottom order

pin.description: set_access: 6–12 digit PIN that opens the doc without login (stored server-side, never synced). Empty string removes it.

login.description: set_access: whether Google/email sign-in is offered (default true).

public.description: set_access: open for anyone with the URL, no login or PIN (default false).

tools.name: bob_notify
tools.title: Notifications to the user
tools.description:
Send a push notification to the signed-in user's own devices (BoB Tools app on phone and web) and read back how they answered.

Use it when you finish background work and need the user's attention or a quick decision — e.g. "3 new leads found", "report is ready", "approve this reply?". Only the user who owns this connection is notified; other people cannot be targeted.

What the user sees: a system notification with your title and body. Tapping it opens the target you set (a doc/dashboard, a table, a record, or a link). On Android and web your action buttons appear on the notification itself; on iOS they appear in the app after the tap. Every notification is also kept in the app's notifications feed, so it is not lost if the push is missed.

Actions:
- send: Push a notification. Params: title, body?, one target of fileId | lineId | url, actions?, reply?, thread?
  Returns notificationId and how many devices were reached. If 0 devices have notifications enabled, the notification is still stored in the feed — tell the user to open the BoB Tools app and allow notifications.
- list: Your notification history, newest first, with read state and the user's answers. Params: thread?, status?, archived?, sinceMs?, beforeMs?, limit? When the result has hasMore=true, call again with beforeMs=nextBeforeMs for the older ones. status=pending returns only questions still waiting for the user — not answered, not resolved, not info. Archived ones are left out unless archived=only or include.
- get: One notification and its answer. Params: notificationId. Returns immediately — it never waits.
- resolve: Close a notification once the matter is settled, with a short note on how it ended. Params: notificationId, note? (up to 500 chars, e.g. "applied", "handled by phone", "no longer relevant"). The buttons and the reply field disappear in the app, the system notification is withdrawn from the user's phones, and a late tap is refused; an answer the user already gave is kept. Its status becomes resolved and it no longer appears in list status=pending. Calling it again only replaces the note. Use it whenever a question you asked stops needing an answer — do not leave it pending.
- update: Change a notification you already sent — new status, text, target or buttons — instead of sending a new one. Params: notificationId? (omitted = your latest sent notification, or the latest in thread if you pass thread — then thread selects the notification and is not changed), then any of title, body, fileId | lineId | url, actions, reply, thread (fields you leave out stay as they are; at least one is required). The result always names the notificationId it updated. The user's devices replace the old notification in place, it becomes unread again, and the previous version is kept in its history (returned by get). If the buttons or the reply mode really change, the user's earlier answer is cleared so they can answer again (the old answer stays in history); passing the same buttons again with a new text keeps the answer. Counts toward the send limit.
  IMPORTANT: to report progress or a new status of something you already notified about ("scan started" → "scan done: 3 leads"), call update with that notificationId — do NOT call send again, or the user gets duplicate notifications.
- archive: Clean up the user's feed — move notifications that no longer need attention but are worth keeping (a done report, a settled question, a past result) out of the feed into the archive. Params: notificationIds (up to 100) or notificationId, note? (why, up to 500 chars). A pending question is also resolved, as with resolve; an answer is kept. Still readable with get and list archived=only. An update brings an archived notification back to the feed.
- unarchive: Return archived notifications to the feed. Params: notificationIds or notificationId.
- delete: Remove worthless notifications for good — duplicates, test pings, stale progress messages nobody needs to see again. Params: notificationIds (up to 100) or notificationId. They disappear from the feed, from list and get, and from the user's phones. Prefer archive when in doubt.
  archive, unarchive and delete return a result per id (ok, unchanged, not_found, not_bob_notify, deleted); one call counts as one write however many ids it names.

Status of every notification (get, list): pending — a question (buttons or reply) still waiting; answered — the user answered; info — no buttons and no reply, nothing was asked, nothing to wait for; resolved — you closed it with resolve (a kept answer is still in response). An update that changes the buttons or the reply mode asks anew and reopens a resolved notification.

Reading the answer: a tap on a button or a typed reply is recorded once (first answer wins). `response.actionId` is the id of the button you defined; `response.text` is the free-text reply. The user may answer much later, so do not block on it: call get every 15 seconds for the first 2 minutes after sending, then once a minute until 10 minutes, then once every 5 minutes (an unanswered get tells you the notification's age and when to check next), or — for a background job — skip the polling and call list status=answered with your thread on the next tick. Every get counts toward the daily tool-call limit like any other call.

thread: your own tag for a series of notifications (e.g. "upwork-scan"). Reuse the same tag on every run so list(thread=...) returns just that series and its answers.

Limit: 30 writes (send, update, resolve, archive, unarchive, delete) and 600 list/get reads per hour. bob_notify calls are free: they do not count toward the daily MCP limit and keep working after it is used up.

flags.description:
Manage file sharing and group shares.

Actions:
- list: List shares by file, company, or user. Params: fileId?, companyId?, includeDeleted?, limit?
- get: Get share details. Params: shareId
- create: Create a share link. Params: fileId (not needed for shareType=linkToGroup with groupShareId — an app entry link), shareType?, allowedOperations?, requirePin?, expirationHours?, viewId?, filters?, displayTitle?, showInList?, embedMode?, shareTheme?, showAllFields?, visibleFieldIds?, canAddData?, canEditData?, canViewData?, canDeleteData?, editData?, canAddRecordsInLink?, groupShareId?
- update: Update share settings. Params: shareId, allowedOperations?, requirePin?, expirationHours?, viewId?, filters?, deleted?, displayTitle?, showInList?, enabled?, embedMode?, shareTheme?, showAllFields?, visibleFieldIds?, canAddData?, canEditData?, canViewData?, canDeleteData?, editData?, canAddRecordsInLink?, fieldSettings?

fieldSettings (update): per-share field settings keyed by field ID; each listed field's entry is
replaced wholly (null removes it, unlisted fields keep theirs). An entry may contain
settingsOverride — a PARTIAL FieldSettings JSON that overrides the field's own settings in
this share only. Example (enable multi-entry input just for this share):
{"field_abc": {"settingsOverride": {"multiEntryEnabled": true, "multiEntryFieldIds": ["field_h", "field_c"]}}}
To force-disable: {"field_abc": {"settingsOverride": {"multiEntryEnabled": false}}}

Filter object schema: {fieldId, filterType: "equals"|"multiSelect"|"dateRange", value?, selectedValues?[], dateFrom?, dateTo?, isLocked?}
- delete: Soft-delete a share. Params: shareId
- get_pin: Get or regenerate share PIN. Params: shareId, regenerate?
A group share is a PORTAL: a page of buttons. A button opens either an existing linkShare on a
data file (linkShareId) or a doc/dashboard (docLinkId — a stable link from bob_docs
action=publish; it opens read-only inside the portal, the link itself stays non-public). Create
the linkShares / doc links first, then pass their IDs as buttons.
- create_group: Create group share (company-level). Params: title, companyId, buttons[], enabled?, embedMode?, shareTheme?
- get_group: Get group share details. Params: shareId
- update_group: Update group share. Params: shareId, title?, buttons? (replaces all), enabled?, embedMode?, shareTheme?, app?, accessMode?, blocklist?, allowlist?, allowDomains?, entryShareId?
  Users see a portal as an "app". app = its look, merged partially (null removes a key), e.g.
  {"app": {"accentColor": "#1E88E5", "iconText": "SK", "layout": "grid"}}. See the app parameter.
  Who may open the app is set on its ENTRY LINKS (linkToGroup / emailToGroup shares with groupShareId = this portal), not on the portal: accessMode / blocklist / allowlist / allowDomains apply to entryShareId if given, otherwise to every linkToGroup entry link of the portal (create one first with action=create, shareType=linkToGroup, groupShareId).
